page: Microsoft Azure DS14-8_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the DSv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB L1d cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and 48 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 112.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 14.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 229 GB, and there are no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPUs included.

Benchmark data reveals a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance, Geekbench single-core score, and single-threaded gzip compression, fall into the weak category, with single-threaded bzip3 decompression registering as poor. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations perform at an average level. This average performance is reflected in the stress-ng multi-core CPU test, Geekbench multi-core score, Passmark CPU score, and memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks.

Given the high memory density of 14.0 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require top-tier single-threaded CPU speed. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all perform in the average tier, indicating suitability for relational databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive data processing. Tradeoffs include lower single-core execution speeds and weak performance on medium-sized LLM inference tasks, making it less suitable for compute-heavy single-threaded applications.
